title: Evening (II.11)
hook: the replay of a bad day starts at lights-out; Francis de Sales puts thanks in front of it
tomorrow: no time to pray between class, lifts and practice. or is there?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the morning: thank, remember what the day is for, look ahead, and offer it. The line was plan the day with god.

Lights off, and the replay starts. The thing you said at lunch. The look on someone's face. The message you shouldn't have sent. On a bad day, the mind goes straight to the wreckage. Francis de Sales puts something odd in front of it. His evening exercise, the other bookend to the morning, begins with thanks. Not after the look back. Before it. Even on the days that went badly. Why that order?
screen: `LIGHTS OFF, THE REPLAY STARTS.` → `STRAIGHT TO THE WRECKAGE.` → `WHY THANKS FIRST?`

segments.voice: Start a little earlier than bedtime. Francis suggests a short pause before supper, a few minutes back in God's company, so the day's prayer doesn't stop at breakfast. Then, before sleep, the order he gives. Thanks first: thank God for keeping you through the day. Only then the look back, and he makes it easy: think where you were, who you were with, what you did. Catholics call this the examination of conscience. Whatever good you find, thank God for it. Whatever went wrong, ask his pardon, resolve to confess it when you can, and set it right with care. Then the last step: commend to God's Providence your body and soul, the Church, your family and your friends. Ask Our Lady, your guardian angel and the saints to watch over you, and go to rest with God's blessing. So here's one way to read the puzzle. Thanks first means you never walk into the review empty-handed; the wrong things get looked at from inside a day that also held gifts. And the night doesn't end on the replay. It ends on handing over. The morning offered a day not yet lived. The evening gives back the one that was, good and bad together.
screen: `A PAUSE BEFORE SUPPER.` · `THANKS COMES FIRST.` · `WHERE, WITH WHOM, WHAT.` · `COMMENDED, THEN REST.` · then, large: `HAND HIM THE DAY.`

segments.voice: Count three good things from today on your fingers; small ones count. Then walk back once through where you were and with whom, and name one thing to set right. If you pray, you can hand the people you love to God by name.
Evening. In the Introduction, the day's last exercise: thanks, a look back, pardon asked, and everything handed over before sleep.
Keep this one: hand him the day, the good and the bad in the same two hands. Sleep well.

screen: `DAY 1500 COUNTS.` → `THE DEVOUT LIFE · 9 OF 25.` → `TOMORROW: NO TIME TO PRAY BETWEEN CLASS AND PRACTICE. OR IS THERE?`

notes: Introduction II.11 paraphrased: before supper a short spiritual recollection; before bed, thank God for preserving you that day; examine how you behaved, recalling where, with whom and in what you were occupied; thank God for good found, ask pardon for evil, resolving to confess at the first opportunity and amend; commend body, soul, the Church, relatives and friends to Providence; ask Our Lady, your angel and the saints to watch over you; go to rest with God's blessing.
